entries.title: X-rays tear water apart before its electrons can relax
entries.summary: A single X‑ray photon can break both O–H bonds in a water molecule within a few femtoseconds (quadrillionths of a second), creating neutral atomic oxygen. As shown by a study published in the journal Physical Review Letters, this breakup happens before the electrons finish…

entries.title: Exquisite X-rays and dynamic compression initiate a new era of physics experiments on plutonium
entries.summary: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), Argonne National Laboratory (ANL) and Washington State University (WSU) have conducted the first dynamic compression experiments on plutonium at a national light source facility, the Dynamic Compression Sector (DCS).
